summary: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear.
takeaways: We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size.
We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds.
Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora.
